acceptance_criteria.requirement: Use a rectangular 65 mm × 65 mm board outline (dimension tolerance 0.1 mm) with two copper layers.

Use a six-pin header J1 with pins 1 through 6 assigned ROW1, ROW2, ROW3, COL1, COL2, COL3. The external controller supplies scanning and pull-ups; do not add a controller, supply connector, or pull-up resistors.

Create nine normally-open momentary switches SW11 through SW33 in a three-row, three-column grid. For each position (r,c), connect COLc to one terminal of SWrc, the other switch terminal to the anode of a dedicated diode Drc, and the diode cathode to ROWr. Each switch-diode junction must be its own net.
Use small-signal switching diodes with visible cathode markings. Record diode part numbers and footprint pin mappings. If switches have duplicated terminals, map the terminal pairs correctly.

Place switch centres at x = 12, 32, and 52 mm for columns 1 through 3 and y = 12, 32, and 52 mm for rows 1 through 3, measured from the lower-left corner. Tolerance is 0.5 mm in each axis. Mark each switch RrCc on silkscreen.
Place each diode within 8 mm of its switch centre. Keep all three row nets and all three column nets distinct, connected only through their specified switch-diode branches.
Editable schematic and fully placed and routed PCB are supplied with readable entry files and a README documenting component choices and unresolved requirements.
Header pitch, passive packages, component pin mapping, silkscreen, board containment, copper clearance, trace widths, and complete routing satisfy the common prompt requirements.
